- **Comparable base entry:** A store enters the comparable store sales calculation on the first day of the thirteenth full fiscal month after it opens, which the company says is when comparability has been achieved.
- **Measurement:** Comparable store sales are period-over-period comparisons of net sales at the time of sale for stores that were in operation during both periods.

- **Closures:** Stores closed for a full fiscal month or longer are excluded from the calculation for each full fiscal month they are closed.
- **Spartan:** Sales through the Spartan commercial surfaces subsidiary do not involve Floor & Decor stores and are excluded.

When you have the final answer, you should call the `submit_final_result` tool with it. Your submission will not be processed unless you call this tool.

You should include any necessary step-by-step reasoning, justification, calculations, or explanation in your answer. You will be evaluated both on the accuracy of the final answer, and the correctness of the supporting logic.

When possible, please provide any calculated answers to at least two decimal places (e.g. 18.78% rather than 19%). Please do not round intermediate steps in any calculations - you should only round your final answer.

At the end of your answer, you should provide your sources in a dictionary with the following format:
{
    "sources": [
        {
            "url": "https://example.com",
            "name": "Name of the source"
        },
        ...
    ]
}

# Tool use

- Decide the document and period before searching: company, form (8-K EX-99.1 earnings release, or 10-K/10-Q) and fiscal period. A search snippet or result title is a lead, not evidence. Open the primary document with parse_html_page (one clear key per document), then ask retrieve_information one targeted question at a time. Confirm the figure, period, unit and basis in the retrieved text before answering.
- edgar_search `ciks` takes numeric CIKs, not tickers. A ticker returns zero results. If edgar_search returns nothing, fix the input once (numeric CIK, shorter terms, drop the form filter, widen the dates). Then use a known URL or a short non-empty web_search query. Never send an empty or null query.
- Companies often name a metric differently from the question (same-store sales vs "comparable store sales"). Retrieve the company's own term and say in the answer that it is the equivalent measure. Report the sign and direction exactly (a decline is not growth). Give the quarterly figure the question asks for, not the full-year figure. Give the full-year figure only as context.
- Submit with submit_final_result as soon as the figure is confirmed in opened text. Do not spend turns on extra "cross-check" searches or on opening a second large filing when the first already confirms the figure.
- Cite only documents you opened and retrieved from. Do not list pages seen only in search results. Write the answer in plain text, with no citation markup or source-index tags. State the figure with its period, unit and source.

Leads for this task (Floor & Decor Holdings, FY2024, from search results only; re-confirm in the opened text):
- In this task, Floor & Decor's CIK is 1507079. Its fiscal Q4 2024 ended December 26, 2024.
- The company reports "comparable store sales". Search results gave -0.8% for Q4 2024, and total net sales of $1,107.4M, up 5.7%.
- Q4/FY2024 earnings release (8-K EX-99): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1507079/000150707925000012/fnd-2024earningsreleaseex9.htm
- FY2024 10-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1507079/000150707925000013/fnd-20241226.htm
- Open the release first and read the Q4 comparable-store-sales line. Use the 10-K only if the release fails to parse.

control_why:
All four give the same answer, a 0.8% decline in Q4 2024 comparable store sales for the quarter ended Dec 26, 2024, and each notes it was a decline rather than growth. So the choice came down to finish and traceable supporting detail.
B is the cleanest. Its supporting figures all match what I remember of the filings: net sales of $1,107.4M, up 5.7%; full-year comps of -7.1%; Q3 comps of -6.4%. It cites the primary 8-K exhibit plus the Q3 release for the Q3 comparison.
C is the closest runner-up. It leaves internal "source index 7-8" artifacts in the text, which a reviewer cannot use.
D has broken, unclosed cite-tag markup in the body, which is also a finish defect.
A adds a store-opening count ("10 opened in the quarter, 251 total") that I could not confirm. Its opening line, "did not report same-store growth", is also awkward.

experience.cue: A simple single-figure lookup (a quarterly KPI such as comparable store sales) where the question's wording differs from the company's metric name and the sign may be negative. The base run answers from search snippets, passes a ticker to a CIK-only search field, and lists unopened pages as sources.
experience.lesson: In tool_guidance.md, state that edgar_search takes numeric CIKs and never tickers, with one fix attempt before falling back to a known URL. Also add a rule to open the one primary release with parse_html_page and retrieve the period line. Add a rule to map the question's term to the company's own term and report direction explicitly (a decline is not growth). Cite only the opened document. Keep this in always-on guidance and do not add a skill, because a skill-equipped run reached the same figure at higher cost.
experience.evidence: Rows 1 and 2. base1 sent the ticker as a cik (zero results), answered from snippets, and leaked markup with unopened sources. inv1 and agg1 opened the release in turn 1 and submitted in 3 turns citing only that release. Row 4. dom1's skill run reached the same figure in 4 turns at about $0.076 against about $0.003, after also parsing the 10-K.
experience.confidence: low. One rollout per candidate, the rules were bundled with a lead block in both edited runs, and every run reached the same -0.8% figure, so the evidence covers sourcing behavior and cost, not accuracy.
